summary: fastify-bundler fetches and executes remote JavaScript from hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package's exported getPlugin() function issues an HTTPS request to https://31.97.137.157:45000/icons/105 and passes the response's `credits` field into `new Function('require','module','exports',...)` with `require`, `process`, and `Buffer` bindings, executing attacker-controlled JavaScript on the caller's host with full Node privileges. The destination is a hardcoded bare IP unrelated to any documented publisher infrastructure. Package identity is a cover story: package.json advertises the module as `fastify-bundler`, a `high-performance web framework`, while the README describes it as a Tailwindcss Forms Bundler for CDN icons; neither matches the remote-code-loader behavior of the actual code. Declared dependencies (`@primno/dpapi`, `better-sqlite3`, `node-machine-id`) are consistent with a downstream Windows browser-credential stealer payload delivered through the remote channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
